findings.title: buildDeps return type is still `unknown` in the RuntimeStrategy port interface
findings.rationale: The JSDoc comment at lines 381–388 says the former `unknown` return type is no longer needed (cycle is broken), but the actual signature still declares `: unknown` instead of `: PipelineDeps`. This directly violates the acceptance criterion ('buildDeps の対象 payload signature に domain object を表す unknown が残らない'), TC-022, and tasks.md T-05. The import-cycle that required `unknown` was broken by removing `PipelineDeps.runtimeStrategy`; the port-layer change was not completed.

findings.title: `as PipelineDeps` cast is still present after buildDeps call
findings.rationale: Line 222: `deps = this.runtime.buildDeps(...) as PipelineDeps;`. Because Finding 1 (buildDeps returns `unknown` in the interface) was not resolved, this cast remains necessary. Once the port return type is changed to `PipelineDeps`, this cast can and must be removed. Violates acceptance criterion ('対象境界の `as PipelineDeps` cast が除去される') and TC-021.

findings.title: RoundGitEffectsCapability declares listWorktreeChanges?, commitRoundArtifacts?, digestArtifacts? as optional — violates D6 and tasks.md T-03
findings.rationale: Design D6 requires all capability method signatures to be required (no `?`), with `snapshotMainCheckoutGuard` as the sole documented exception. Tasks.md T-03 lists all five `RoundGitEffectsCapability` methods without `?`. Three methods (`listWorktreeChanges?` line 92, `commitRoundArtifacts?` line 107, `digestArtifacts?` line 122) carry the `?` modifier, causing `parallel-review-round.ts` to use method-presence checks (`deps.roundGitEffects?.listWorktreeChanges`, `deps.roundGitEffects.commitRoundArtifacts?.()`) instead of the field-presence pattern mandated by D6. The managed-runtime fake in `managed-runtime-capabilities.test.ts` already implements no-op versions of all three methods, so making them required is directly feasible.

findings.title: LocalRuntime._latestBuiltDeps side-channel: finalizeStepArtifacts implicitly depends on composition root having set deps.pushCapability post-buildDeps
findings.rationale: finalizeStepArtifacts reads `this._latestBuiltDeps` to obtain `pushCapability` that runner.ts sets on the deps object after buildDeps() returns (JavaScript reference semantics). This undocumented precondition: (1) is invisible from the StepArtifactLifecycleCapability interface, (2) causes a runtime throw if capability is called before buildDeps, and (3) imposes an implicit ordering contract between the composition root and the capability. The design spec does not document this pattern. Options: extend CommitPushInfra to carry pushCapability (eliminates the side channel), or explicitly document and add a test asserting the precondition.

options.label: Extend CommitPushInfra to include pushCapability
options.consequence: Eliminates the side channel entirely; callers thread pushCapability through the infra struct; requires updating commitAndPush callers.

options.label: Document and test the precondition
options.consequence: Keeps the current pattern but adds a contract test asserting buildDeps must be called before finalizeStepArtifacts on LocalRuntime; lower change impact.

The PipelineDeps field is correctly `roundGitEffects`, not `runtimeStrategy`. The variable name is a legacy naming artifact but does not inject a `runtimeStrategy` field into deps.

findings.title: RuntimeStrategy.buildDeps port interface still returns `unknown` instead of `PipelineDeps`
findings.rationale: The JSDoc comment at lines 381-388 correctly states the return type should be PipelineDeps (import cycle broken by types.ts no longer importing RuntimeStrategy), but the actual return type on line 394 was never changed from `unknown` to `PipelineDeps`. Violates acceptance criterion ('buildDeps の対象 payload signature に domain object を表す unknown が残らない'), TC-022, and tasks.md T-05. Fix: add `import type { PipelineDeps } from "../types.js"` and change `: unknown` to `: PipelineDeps`.

findings.title: `as PipelineDeps` cast still present at runner.ts:222
findings.rationale: Because RuntimeStrategy.buildDeps still declares unknown as its return type (Finding 1), the cast `this.runtime.buildDeps(...) as PipelineDeps` remains necessary. Once Finding 1 is resolved, this becomes a plain typed assignment. Violates acceptance criterion ('対象境界の as PipelineDeps cast が除去される') and TC-021.

findings.title: `_latestBuiltDeps` side-channel not removed; `CommitPushInfra` not extended with `pushCapability` (decision: option a)
findings.rationale: The human-supplied decision selected option (a): extend CommitPushInfra with `pushCapability?: PushCapability | null` and eliminate the `_latestBuiltDeps` instance field. Neither action has been implemented. `_latestBuiltDeps` (line 161) is still assigned in buildDeps (line 644) and read in finalizeStepArtifacts (line 766). CommitPushInfra in commit-push.ts:66-86 has no `pushCapability` field. This imposes an invisible ordering precondition: buildDeps must be called before finalizeStepArtifacts or the runtime throws. Fix: add `pushCapability` to CommitPushInfra, thread it from the StepExecutor call site, use `infra.pushCapability` inside finalizeStepArtifacts, then delete `_latestBuiltDeps`.

findings.title: `RoundGitEffectsCapability` has three optional methods violating D6 and tasks.md T-03
findings.rationale: Methods `listWorktreeChanges?` (line 92), `commitRoundArtifacts?` (line 106), and `digestArtifacts?` (line 121) are declared optional on the interface. Design D6 requires all capability methods to be required (only `snapshotMainCheckoutGuard` is excepted). Tasks.md T-03 lists all five methods without `?`. As a result, parallel-review-round.ts uses method-presence checks (`deps.roundGitEffects?.digestArtifacts`, `deps.roundGitEffects?.listWorktreeChanges`, `await deps.roundGitEffects.commitRoundArtifacts?.()`) instead of the D6-mandated field-presence pattern. ManagedRuntime already provides no-op implementations for all three methods, so making them required requires no new implementations. Fix: remove `?` from the three methods; update parallel-review-round.ts callers to use field-presence checks.

findings.title: as PipelineDeps cast present — TC-021 non-compliant
findings.rationale: TC-021 (must) requires no `as PipelineDeps` cast in runner.ts. Line 222 reads: `deps = this.runtime.buildDeps(config, request, slug, workspace) as PipelineDeps;`. The cast is still present. The root cause is that the RuntimeStrategy port interface declares buildDeps returning `unknown` (runtime-strategy.ts), so CommandRunner cannot receive a typed value without casting. Previous reviewers (iter 3, conformance-result-001) incorrectly confirmed this as passing.

findings.title: RuntimeStrategy.buildDeps returns unknown — TC-022 non-compliant
findings.rationale: TC-022 (must) requires the RuntimeStrategy port interface to declare buildDeps returning PipelineDeps. The current signature returns `unknown`, with a comment 'buildDeps() returns unknown to avoid a ports→domain import cycle per DSM §3. Callers in domain (CommandRunner) assert the result as PipelineDeps.' The DSM §3 constraint is real but does not exempt the implementation from TC-022; the design must resolve the cycle (e.g., via a BuildDepsResult interface in ports, or relocating PipelineDeps). Architecture doc components.md:175 claims the port returns PipelineDeps but this is incorrect for the interface — only the concrete implementations do.

findings.title: TC-T15-05 does not prove its stated compile-time invariant
findings.rationale: TC-T15-05 is labeled 'buildDeps return type — compile-time proof' and the comment states 'If buildDeps returned unknown, this assignment would require an as PipelineDeps cast.' However, the test only assigns `const deps: PipelineDeps = makeBaseDeps()` — a direct construction of a PipelineDeps-shaped object, not a call through the RuntimeStrategy port interface. This trivially compiles regardless of whether the port declares `unknown`. The actual production path `this.runtime.buildDeps(...)` is never exercised by this test. Prior reviewers relied on this test as evidence that TC-022 passes, contributing to the incorrect conformance conclusions.

findings.title: Terminal publication breaks the documented cwd fallback
findings.rationale: PipelineDeps inherits StepContext's contract that omitted cwd falls back to process.cwd(), and the previous LocalRuntime.commitFinalState implementation honored it. The new awaiting-archive, awaiting-resume, and fidelity-gate halt calls pass an empty string instead. A backward-compatible caller omitting cwd therefore persists terminal state locally but runs terminal git publication with an invalid cwd; best-effort handling can hide the failure, leaving the remote checkpoint/finalize state unpublished. Restore process.cwd() fallback at all three call sites or in the adapter and add an omitted-cwd test.

findings.title: Terminal publication cwd fallback uses empty string instead of process.cwd()
findings.rationale: Both commitFinalState call sites (lines 399 and 623) use `deps.cwd ?? ""` as the fallback. StepContext declares `cwd?: string` as optional with a documented contract that absence SHALL fall back to `process.cwd()` (step-context.ts:14,20). When deps.cwd is undefined, an empty string is passed to commitFinalState instead of process.cwd(). No omitted-cwd terminal publication test was added. The process.cwd() fallback was never restored.
